newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan traders expect more Russian PGM spot sales.
newsitem.headline: Japan traders expect more Russian PGM spot sales.

text.p: Russia is expected to continue selling platinum group metals (PGMs) in the spot market, especially palladium, taking advantage of current high prices, Japanese precious metal traders said on Monday.

"As the contracted volume of PGMs to Japanese clients this year is lower than last year, I think Russia wants to sell in mass, especially palladium, to profit from current higher prices," a senior official of a major bullion house said.

Recently, Russia's platinum group metal export agency, Almazjuvelirexport, has been selling PGMs, palladium in particular, to some Japanese clients in the spot market, traders said. The size of the sales was unknown.

Traders said that Russia may aggressively sell palladium in the spot market, but that substantial sales of platinum were unlikely, based on suspicions that Russia's platinum supplies could be drying up.
They also said it was hard to think that Russia was sacrificing contractual platinum group metal (PGM) shipments in favour of spot sales.
"Russia has an obligation to supply PGM metals to their clients. I don't think Russia gives priority to spot sales," a Japanese trader said.

An analyst in New York said last Friday the fact that the Russians are returning to the spot market suggests they may be bypassing contractual obligations to get the highest price, which could be indication they may not have a lot to sell, especially in the case of platinum.

After a suspension of more than six months in Russian PGM exports, the first palladium shipments under long-term contracts for 1997 arrived in Japan in early July, and the first platinum shipments late last week, traders said.
